text: A website for my cafe.

@Requester The brief is too open to write a checkable charter. Four quick questions.
1. What is the main job of the site?
   Option 1: Show menu, hours and location
   Option 2: Take table reservations
   Option 3: Take online orders
   Option 4: Tell the cafe's story and build the brand
2. Who is the main visitor?
   Option 1: Local regulars and walk-ins
   Option 2: Tourists and newcomers
   Option 3: Office workers ordering ahead
   Option 4: Event and group bookers
3. Which sections must the site include?
   Option 1: Menu with prices
   Option 2: Opening hours and map
   Option 3: Photo gallery
   Option 4: Contact form or phone and email
4. Any hard rules on name, language, look or content (for example cafe name, brand colors, languages, things to avoid)?

It's called Brew Lab, in Indiranagar. Show the menu with prices, opening hours 8am to 10pm every day, and our location. People should be able to pre-order coffee for pickup. Warm, modern, mobile-first.
@Adaptation Charter recorded for Brew Lab. Menu items, prices, street address and where pre-orders are sent are open inputs, shown as marked placeholders.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 8 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority Three small workflows, in build order, 70 of 100 budget: core page, menu with placeholders, pre-order form. Menu items, prices, address and order destination stay marked placeholders. No payment is built. The order summary shows on the page only, since no delivery channel is supplied. Leaves 30 for rework.

proposal.name: Core page: header, hours, location and warm mobile-first styling
proposal.goal_gap: Site v0 has no Brew Lab header, hours, location or styling.
proposal.expected_outcome: A single HTML file with a viewport tag, a Brew Lab title and header, an hours section (8am to 10pm, every day), a location section naming Indiranagar, Bengaluru with a map link and a marked street address placeholder, and a warm mobile-first palette with no fixed widths that cause sideways scroll at 375px.
outputs: index.html with header, hours and location sections and inline CSS
proposal.completion_check: Title and header read Brew Lab; hours text says 8am to 10pm every day; location names Indiranagar, Bengaluru with a map link and a visible address placeholder; viewport meta present; base CSS is for small screens with min-width media queries; no horizontal scroll at 375px.

proposal.name: Menu section with marked placeholders
proposal.goal_gap: No menu section exists, and no menu items or prices have been supplied.
proposal.expected_outcome: A menu section listing drinks, each with a price, where every item and price not supplied is a visibly marked placeholder, such as 'Item name (placeholder)' and 'Price: TBC'. Item data is held in one JavaScript array so the order form can reuse it.
outputs: Menu section and menu data array in index.html
proposal.completion_check: The menu section renders at least 4 drink rows, each with a price field, and every unsupplied name or price is visibly marked as a placeholder. No invented real prices appear.

proposal.name: Pre-order form with order summary
proposal.goal_gap: Visitors cannot pre-order coffee for pickup.
proposal.expected_outcome: A pre-order form where a visitor picks menu items and quantities, enters name and phone number, and picks a pickup time between 8am and 10pm. On submit it validates the inputs and shows an order summary on the page. No payment and no sending.
outputs: Pre-order form and submit handler in index.html
proposal.completion_check: The form has item and quantity inputs fed from the menu data, name and phone fields, and a time input limited to 08:00 to 22:00. Submitting a valid order shows a summary with items, quantities, name, phone and pickup time. A time outside 8am to 10pm is rejected. No payment fields exist.

text: @Adaptation GRANT all three at the rate-card cost of 70, leaving 30 uncommitted. Each envelope allows one retry; a failed retry stops the run. The 30 reserve covers up to three fixes at 8 each. Trade-off: no money for a gallery or extra sections, which the brief did not ask for.

@Requester The goal is reached: Brew Lab is built as one HTML file, and all 8 done-when items passed Audit on site v3. It shows the menu, 8am to 10pm hours every day, an Indiranagar location with a map link, and a pre-order form with an on-page order summary. It is mobile-first, with no horizontal overflow at 360px or 1280px. Caveat: Audit checked the pre-order submit by reading the code, not by running a submission. Still placeholders, because you have not supplied them: drink names and prices, street address and map pin, phone number, where pre-orders should be sent (the summary currently shows on the page only, nothing is sent to the cafe), and brand colours, logo and photos. Send any of these and I will have them added. Until pre-orders have a delivery channel, the cafe will not receive them.

Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence.
